q_and_a.question: What is the first memory you have of your main character as a child, and what emotions do you associate with it?
q_and_a.answer: the first memory i have is of my aunt kathy. i was playing with brissel blocks and i couldnt't put some together and i remember she helped me out. I remember a lot of time with my uncle george and aunt kathy. they were my parents best friends. i don't really have any negative emotions related to my uncle george and aunt kathy. my family was very into church and that was their entire community so my uncle and aunt are very religious; the type that would always say they'll pray for you, but then genuinely pray for everyone they said they would. we weren't as close by the times I came out so they never had a real impact in my life at that point to worry about their reactions. one of their son's i am 95% sure he is gay but he instead just keeps it a secret and I think it was because of how my uncle would respond, but they've never brought it upwith me at all even though they knew about it. wow that was an obscure memory. my uncle just called me so i think that's why it's so fresh.

outline_point: * Growing up in a family that rejected him for being gay

q_and_a.question: What was the first time you remember feeling different from your family, and how did you process that experience?
q_and_a.answer: I was adopted so I always knew I was different. I never liked girls the way other boys did so I knew I was different but I was afraid to say anything because I was always taught it was one of the worst things a person could be.  I had a household where my dad would yell at the tv and i distinctively remember him calling madonna a whore and a witch and he would always get so bent out of shape because people were different and didn't adhere to the world "according tbob miller"

q_and_a.question: How did your sense of self-worth change over time as a result of being rejected by your family?
q_and_a.answer: it was awful.  it took me well into my adult ages to start to find my self-worth.  It's sad because they always told me I was special and coudl do anything I wanted to and that I was so smart and was more sensitive to others and I have such a big heart and when they thought I was a christian it was a blessing and a gift, but when i became my true self it was me being arrogant an something was wrong with me and i'm just angry and hateful because i now point out the hypocrisy

q_and_a.question: Can you describe the physical sensations you associate with feelings of shame or isolation in this context?
q_and_a.answer: i feel a need for comfort, yet I don't want people around me.  I wnat to be alone because I have issues trusting what people tell me is true at face value.  I would always try to run away because after being kicked out, and completely unaccepted by my family it completely destroyed my self value and self worth.  I wasn't able to go to college because I had to get a job and get my GED so I have an intellect with no formal education.  I am smarter than most of my peers but I don't have anything behind it. I find it hard to complete things and I have a lot of gaps in my adult skills because at 16 instead of worrying about college, I was worrying about paying rent and feeding myself.

outline_point: * Rejection from his parents, leading to instability and searching for new relationships and places to live

q_and_a.question: How did your protagonist feel when he received news of rejection from his parents?
q_and_a.answer: devastated. like his whole world was over.  anger at his brother for influencing them. violent anger because he aligned with so much of their values, however a core part of his being was being rejected. a hardwired part of him that simply was a part of him.  he was held to different standards than everyone else.  he was adopted and he felt extra-betrayed.  they committed to raising him and loving him as their own, yet he wondered why they would reject him for this.  he was angered they even dared to adopt him when their love was so conditional yet the preached unconditional love.

q_and_a.question: Can you describe the physical sensation in his body as he processed their decision?
q_and_a.answer: nausa, hot flashes, dizziness, the taste of adrenaline

q_and_a.question: What was the most difficult thing about being rejected by people who were supposed to love him unconditionally?
q_and_a.answer: it shattered my world view.  it shattered my idea that people are good at the core.  it made me realize that although I did everythign they told me to, that faith; that spirituality and that connection, were never there.  I spent many years angry, bitter, and lost burning bridges with others and not taking accountability for anything; why should I have? I took accountability and I lost my family, my house, my stability, my ability to love.  I then stopped looking at people as connections and equals and had a bitter and jaded view of only seeing others as tools.  hindsight I am so grateful I was able to pull myself out of that and it appals me to think I was ever thinking like that, but I see the reason was because of the religious abuse and familial abuse I experienced.

q_and_a.question: How did his living situation change after the rejection, and what sensory details stand out about that new environment?
q_and_a.answer: my parents forced me to move to my sister's house and i had to go to church for youth group, bible studies, and sundays.  i wasn't allowed to have any of my former frieinds because they were a "bad influence" on me.  after a while they "let me" move home but when they found out I had a boyfriend they kicked me out again.  I stayed at my friend brandie's for a while with her mom and brother, and then after a few weeks I moved in with her girlfriend Wendy, and started renting a room from wendy, colleen (her OTHER girlfriend... such a messy situation), and my friend nate who was one of my first gay friends I had met online, and he had ended up moving to my area because he was also in a bad situation.  I switched from high school to independent studies where I had to go once a week to meet with teachers and turnin my homework.  I was working at tacobell just to survive.

q_and_a.question: What was the emotional trigger that made him start seeking out new relationships to fill the void left by his parents?
q_and_a.answer: i felt alone.  I had friends that were there for me and helped me out.  I was very defensive and very broken.  I needed some help and the people that I was told were going to destroy me were the ones that were there for me.  It was a long confusing time.  It took years of healing to get past a lot of these things.

q_and_a.question: What was the most meaningful relationship from your protagonist's past that is influencing their current actions?
q_and_a.answer: DJ, my current partner.  we have been together for over 18 years.  He was the kindest most beautiful soul when I met him.  he truly changed my life and has always been there for me.  he accepts me with open arms and genuinely gives me the benefit of the doubt in everything. he always has my side and has been there with me through everything in life including my dad dying recently.  he is my rock and everything I became and all the live's I've touched wouldn't have been psosible iwthout his unconditional love.

q_and_a.answer: he was direct about thinking i was cute and then continued the conversation trying to get to know me

q_and_a.question: Can you recall any specific moments where you felt like you were being seen or understood by DJ?
q_and_a.answer: all the time now.  when i have been going through losing my dad right now, when i lost my biological mom in 2016, my current fight with my sister, before with my parents the first time i saw them in many years, he was with me.  he always listens to me and always has my side. he's always there to listen and always makes sure i protect myself.  when i have ideas he listens and tells me if they're good, and encourages me to reaech for the stars.  he never loses faith in me and always believes in me even when i don't believe in myself.  he's a true unicorn. he's like the type of person that was a muse in legends and you think people like him are not real, but he is.

outline_point: * DJ walks into his office at work with Chinese takeout, and they start dating

q_and_a.question: What did the aroma of the Chinese takeout remind him of from his childhood?
q_and_a.answer: i'm not sure it was from childhood, but i think it was just his favorite chinese food in sacramento. in fact it remained his favorite which is funny because i wasn't a big fan of it soo when he would get Good Friends, I would get jamba juice next door usually. but now that we live in san francisco we have all kinds of really amazing chinese options and we go frequently.

q_and_a.question: How did the sight of DJ walking in with food affect the coworker who had a crush on them?
q_and_a.answer: she didn't have a crush, she was actually a lesbian but she said eh was so cute and sexy i could take the rest of the day off and have a good weekend. so then i left and went with him for the weekend.

q_and_a.question: What subtle gesture or expression would indicate that DJ's intentions were more than just friendly?
q_and_a.answer: we just spoke and he told me his intentions. we could feel it. it was a look. we both just knew.

outline_point: **V. Life with DJ**

q_and_a.question: How would you describe the sounds of DJ's daily routine, and what do they reveal about his personality?
q_and_a.answer: he has evolved. he's the type of person that rolls out of bed 20 minutes before he's supposed to arrive somewhere and then gets there 30 minutes late. it actually drives me INSANE and so i'm the one nagging and pushing and getting us out the door.  for the first time ever, he was on time to my own bithday brunch last year. it only took 16 years hahaha

q_and_a.question: What is the first thing DJ notices when he wakes up in the morning, and how does it affect him?
q_and_a.answer: when i'm home, he ususally tells me he loves me and that i'm beautiful.

q_and_a.question: In what ways has living with DJ changed your protagonist's sense of identity or self-perception?
q_and_a.answer: even when I don't see myself, DJ sees me and he makes sure I know I'm loved.  he goes above and beyond to be a good person but yet he is genuine that way and it is such a breath of fresh air.

outline_point: * Moves in with DJ and eventually stays there for 18 years

q_and_a.question: Can you describe the first impression of the house when your character moved in?
q_and_a.answer: well DJ's sister lived there who she's an awful person now, but that's a whole other story.  His best friend Dante and his mom also lived there. It was an odd living situation and it took me a long time to understand how someone's Mom would live with their son and it seemed so weird and unacceptable to me for so many years.  Dante's relationship with his mom was always weird to me but as an adult I now know that they have an actual healthy relationship and it was so foreign to me because my relationship with my parents was anything but healthy.  It took me a long time to see the status quo in my family was wrong and dysfunctional.

q_and_a.question: What was their initial reaction to living with a person they didn't know well, like DJ?
q_and_a.answer: well DJ does what he wants regardless of anyone else's concerns.  But his friends didnt' like me at first. in fact it took us all a long time to genuinely start to care for each other.  now i love all of his friends like my own.

q_and_a.question: How did their daily life change as they settled into this new environment?
q_and_a.answer: everyone did their own thing for the most part, people had different jobs, and we all had our own life but yet we would hang out at home. watch anime and play video games.

outline_point: * Notes that he had a lot of growing to do still, especially after being kicked out of his family home at 16

q_and_a.question: How did the protagonist feel about himself in that moment when he was kicked out of the family home?
q_and_a.answer: like everythign was over and completely ended. my future was non-existent and my family didnt' love me anymore.  I didn't feel worthy of love and I didn't think god loved me either.

q_and_a.question: What physical sensations came over him as he packed up his belongings and left the only home he had ever known?
q_and_a.answer: nausaea, panic, sorrow, extreme anger at my family, disappointment, more anger of their hypocrisy. I still carry some of that today, it never completely goes away.

q_and_a.question: What memories or emotions lingered for him as he walked away from the house for the last time?
q_and_a.answer: I realized I hated my family. they were awful people that didn't accept anyone outside of their bubble.  their fears and phobias controlled what they did, but they went above and beyond to be "good people" to those in their circle and a few people outside of it, but they lacked any actual positive action to make the world a better place or to actually show unconditional love.
